faq.q: What is Delta's current Official Community Plan?
faq.a: The Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), "Housing Our Future", adopted by Delta Council on July 8, 2024 — a single consolidated plan whose Land Use Plan (s. 1.5, Map 2) sets the designations for the whole city.

faq.q: Is there still a Tsawwassen Area Plan or a Ladner Area Plan in Delta's OCP?
faq.a: No. Those were schedules of the previous OCP, Bylaw No. 3950 (the Tsawwassen Area Plan was Schedule D.1). Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) superseded them with one consolidated plan — there is no Schedule D.1 in the current OCP.

faq.q: How do I find what can be built on a Delta property?
faq.a: Check the property's OCP designation in the Land Use Plan (s. 1.5.1 designations, applied on Map 2), then its zone on the zoning maps that form part of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600, then whether a Development Permit Area applies — all three layers govern.

faq.q: What did SSMUH change on Delta's single-family lots?
faq.a: Delta introduced the provincially required zoning updates allowing up to four units on all single-detached and duplex lots, as part of the framework the 2024 OCP provides for Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing.

faq.q: What does the Agriculture (A) designation mean?
faq.a: In the OCP's s. 1.5.1 designations, Agriculture (A) is the designation applied on Map 2 to maintain agricultural lands; where the land is also in the Agricultural Land Reserve, ALC rules on residences and uses apply on top of the City's A-zone zoning.
